title: The use of phrases like 'hardworking mother' or vague references to a 'bright future' for children may slow funding for women.
Identifying a child in the profile photo may accelerate funding for female borrowers.
Explicit mentions of repayment or repayment promises may slow funding for female borrowers.
Female borrowers who use abstract development goals like food security may fund more slowly.
Direct appeals for funding may slow funding speed for male borrowers.
Mentioning the loan amount in local currency may slow funding speed for female borrowers.
Mentioning widowhood or employing dramatic narrative framing regarding personal struggle may slow funding for female borrowers.
Female borrowers who provide a specific count of children may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention specific family challenges or financial instability may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who list specific monthly income may fund faster.
Mentioning specific institutional or brand names predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who list specific products or goals beyond family welfare fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention benefits to their family or community fund faster.
Mentioning benefits for children predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Specifying the number of years a business has operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Longer pitch text predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention their husband's role or family structure fund faster.
Female borrowers who express explicit gratitude in their pitches fund more slowly.
